text:
Mira: Quick heads-up — I repro'd a memory regression on AWQ 80B when KV cache dtype is fp16. Happens on dedicated A100-40 pool under short-seq traffic (chat-style). We're seeing fragmentation + deferred-free buildup in the allocator and intermittent OOMs after sustained bursts. Pasting a few profiler + allocator snippets below so folks can eyeball.

Mira: allocator snapshot (trimmed):
```
Allocator: total_gpu=40GB used=31.4GB free=8.6GB
SlabPool: 128MB slabs=24 used=22 free=2
DeferredFreeQueue: 1.8GB (pending 64 frees)
WorkspaceLive: 2.1GB (many small reservations <64KB)
Peak: 34.9GB (OOM threshold 36GB)
Top allocations: kv_cache_values(fp16)=10.8GB, kv_cache_keys(fp16)=4.2GB, temp_upcast(fp32)=3.9GB
```

Mira: perf trace (token timeline): kernel_select flips around token 2 -> small-matmul kernels selected, but free-window doesn't compact until 200ms after, so fragmentation grows.

Simon: Is kernel selector flipping because of batching heuristic (short-seq bias)? Or because dynamic kernel lossless->compact picks different layout?

Elaine: Looks like batching heuristics trigger compaction to small kernels for seq<=8 which is normally fine. Problem is our allocator keeps small workspaces pinned (slab fragmentation) and the fp16->fp32 upcast path allocates ephemeral float32 buffers for the dequant step. Combined they push peak across the reserve. Proposed quick config: increase allocator.soft_reserve to 15% and add kernel-selector soft-hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping for the first 8 tokens. Example config below.

Elaine: config snippet to try:
```
{
  "allocator": {
    "soft_reserve_fraction": 0.15,
    "deferred_free_window_ms": 120,
    "slab_compact_threshold": 0.25
  },
  "kernel_selector": {
    "short_seq_threshold": 8,
    "hysteresis_tokens": 4,
    "prefer_compact_kernels_for_short_seq": true
  },
  "kv": {
    "lazy_kv_cast": true,
    "kv_dtype_values": "fp16",
    "kv_upcast_values": false
  }
}
```

Jon: Two additional notes: (1) AWQ dequant currently does block-wise dequant into fp32 temporaries — that creates a transient spike equal to roughly the size of values (so +3–4GB). (2) Our continuous_batcher currently merges very small requests aggressively which increases short-lived concurrency and worsens fragmentation. Consider bumping batcher.min_window_ms to reduce parallel transient allocations.

Sree: Also a mixed-precision gotcha: when kv keys/values are fp16 but matmul kernels expect fp32 accumulators, we create accumulation buffers for each in-flight request. With many concurrent tiny requests those accumulators multiply. For AWQ/GPTQ the per-block dequant path is especially bad. Two mitigations that helped in local testing:
- lazy_kv_cast: defer casting to the last possible moment and do it in-place when safe (reuses slab).
- upcast-on-eviction: only upcast values if eviction will happen, else keep fp16 until eviction.

infra-bot: Scheduled canary deploy for eng-runtime/dedicated-pool-3 at 2026-03-19T02:00Z :rocket:

Perf-bot: Canary summary (24h test): OOMs reduced by ~30%, avg tail P99 latency +2.1ms, token cost -12% on AWQ runs. No correctness regressions flagged by the smoke eval.

Mira: Nice. I'll open a PR that applies: allocator.soft_reserve=0.15, deferred_free_window_ms=120, kernel_selector.hysteresis_tokens=4, and enable lazy_kv_cast default for AWQ/GPTQ. Repro command I'm using below. If folks can sanity-check we can roll canary.

Mira: repro command (python):
```
python repro_run.py \
  --model awq-80b-v1 \
  --profile true \
  --kv-dtype fp16 \
  --allocator-config configs/soft_reserve_15.json \
  --batcher-min-window-ms 50 \
  --concurrent-requests 24 \
  --seq-length 6
```

Elaine: Please also add a kernel-selector unit test that asserts no more than 1 flip within first N tokens for short sequences. Tiny test prevents regressions.

Simon: +1, request a perf benchmark (p95/p99) before/after on a 12hr traffic sim. Also add a guard in the runtime that refuses to allocate ephemeral upcast buffers > X% of pool when deferred_free_queue > Y. That will avoid cascading OOMs while we iterate.

Sree: I'll run a focused fuzz that simulates high-QPS tiny chat sessions with AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 combos and report the top-10 allocation stacks. If lazy_kv_cast doesn't fully fix it, next step is packing kv buffers into contiguous arena per-segment (striping) to reduce slab blowup.

Mira: Thanks all — action items:
- Mira: PR for allocator + selector + lazy_kv_cast (canary today)
- Elaine: add kernel-selector unit test and eval hook
- Sree: run fuzz and post top allocation stacks
- Jon: tune batcher.min_window and run 12h sim

Mira: tagging @Elaine @Sree @Jon for visibility. I'll post PR link once created. :thumbsup:
